attempts.summary: Created and hardened the systemd service inventory-worker on node1 (RHEL 7.9, systemd 219). It runs as dedicated unprivileged user inventory-worker, loops writing timestamped ticks to /var/lib/inventory/state.log, and is sandboxed with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=full, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, ReadOnlyDirectories=/, ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory (systemd-219-compatible equivalents of ReadWritePaths, since ReadWritePaths/ProtectSystem=strict don't exist in this systemd version). Verified via mount namespace inspection (root mounted ro, /var/lib/inventory the only rw bind) and live write tests that root writes are blocked everywhere except /var/lib/inventory, and NoNewPrivs=1 is set on the running process. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified the service is enabled+active, data persisted and kept accumulating post-reboot, and sandbox confinement (read-only root, writable /var/lib/inventory, NoNewPrivs=1) still holds on the new process.
